mechanism_narrative: The level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) has a negative linear relationship with S&P 500 20-day forward returns: lower rates compress discount rates and boost equity valuations, leading to positive returns when rates are low.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0% are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 245.0 signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when CPIAUCSL is above 245.0 are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.0% and housing starts (HOUST) are above 1100.0, it indicates a strong economy with low unemployment and robust housing demand, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods meeting the trigger condition are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle defined by FEDFUNDS above 2.0% and CPIAUCSL above 240.0, the Federal Reserve's policy response to inflation leads to higher discount rates and reduced equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods meeting the trigger condition are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that supports corporate profit growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when UNRATE is below 4.0% are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0, it indicates a weakening manufacturing sector, which signals economic slowdown and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods when INDPRO is below 100.0 are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1000.0, it signals weak residential demand, which is a leading indicator of economic weakness and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods when HOUST is below 1000.0 are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real personal consumption expenditure (RSAFS) above 480000.0 signals strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods when RSAFS is above 480000.0 are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
